SAFETY INSTRUCTIONS
AIRBUS A330-300
EXIT
PLEASE DO NOT REMOVE THIS CARD FROM THE AIRCRAFT
QB55245-1

ADDITIONAL SAFETY INFORMATION
CHANGING SEATS BEFORE TAKE-OFF
It is essential you remain in your allocated
seats for take-off. The seat you are
allocated affects the balance of the
aircraft and can have a critical impact on
the aircraft centre of gravity. If you wish
to move, you must wait till after take-off,
when the seatbelt sign is turned off. You
must also return to your seat for landing.
EXIT ROW SEATING RESTRICTIONS
Certain categories of passengers,
including children, infants, the elderly,
disabled persons, medical cases, and
others who are not able-bodied, are
restricted from occupying the seats at
exits. The reason for these restrictions is
to ensure that in an evacuation, neither
the people at the exit row, or other
passengers, are disadvantaged in their
ability to get out quickly
UNSECURED BAGGAGE IS
A SAFETY RISK
All carry on baggage including
passengers personal effects shall be
stowed either in the overhead lockers or
under the seat in front of you. Do not
stow it under your feet or in the exit
rows. Unsecured baggage can turn into
a lethal missile in an accident or severe
turbulence. In the event of an emergency
evacuation, leave everything behind.
The number one priority is to evacuate
as quickly as possible. Taking carry on
baggage will slow down the evacuation
time on the slides and can cause injury.
If cabin baggage exceeds the allowed
size or weight, it must be checked in
with your other baggage and not carried
in the aircraft cabin.
FLAT LEATHER SHOES ARE BEST
Leather shoes with flat heels are best in
an emergency. Always keep them on for
take off and landing. If you are required to
leave the aircraft in an emergency, your
shoes will provide protection for your feet
when you are outside the aircraft. Do not
wear high heeled shoes as they can
hinder your movement over uneven
surfaces and can also puncture an
evacuation slide. If you do wear high
heels, take them off prior to going down
the escape slide.
PASSENGER SAFETY
INFORMATION CARD
No matter how often you fly, always study
this safety information card prior to take
off and before landing. It is particularly
useful to have this information fresh in
your mind during the flight as safety
equipment and instructions vary from one
aircraft type to another.
FITTING AN OXYGEN MASK
If the aircraft should suffer a rapid loss
of cabin pressure, the oxygen levels
within the cabin will decrease in a
matter of seconds. An oxygen mask will
automatically drop down from above
your head. Put it on immediately by
pulling the mask down firmly towards
you. This will start the flow of oxygen.
JUMP AND SIT ONTO THE
EVACUATION SLIDE
Inflatable escape slides are found at all
doors and all over-wing exits. See the
diagram in the centre section of this card
which shows the exits on this aircraft.
When using an escape slide, fold your
arms across your chest and JUMP onto the
slide, then sit with your feet and legs
together. Do not use your arms to slow
you down, as this could result in painful
burns. Sit upright and look at where you
are going. Once you have reached the
ground, immediately move away from
the aircraft.
DANGEROUS GOODS
Mace and pepper sprays are never
allowed on any aircraft, not even in your
checked luggage. These are considered
weapons and are banned on aircraft
Helium filled balloons cannot be carried
on board an aircraft, as they are likely to
explode inflight due to the change in air
pressure.
Aerosols (including hair sprays, perfumes,
colognes and medicines containing
alcohol) may be carried as toiletries, each
item must not be more than 500 mls.
(Maximum total 2 litres per passenger),
carrying more than this amount is illegal.
RESTRICTIONS ON THE USE OF ELECTRONIC DEVICES
Electronic devices may affect the operation of the aircraft
instruments and systems. Please observe the restrictions listed below.
Prohibited at all times
onboard the aircraft. Devices
which emit electromagnetic
signals such as:
Transceivers, FM/AM radios,
pocket pagers, radio controlled
devices, printers, television
receivers, audio equipment with
wireless controls and Furby toys.
Prohibited at all times except
during boarding of the aircraft
at the direction of the crew.
Mobile / Cellular telephones.
Restricted from use during
take-off and climb
(approximately 20 minutes)
and must be switched off
immediately the aircraft starts
descent for landing:
Video cameras*, video players,
cassette players, CD players,
pocket computer games,
electronic note-books,
headphone stereo players,
personal computers, word
processors, electric shavers.
Not restricted from use at
anytime medical appliances
such as:
Hearing Aids; pacemakers,
medical appliances that have
prior approval by Qantas and
watches & cameras* with built
in batteries.
* Use of audio or visual recording equipment except for personal use must have
prior approval by Qantas Public Affairs.
